Rakesh's rank from the start = 42 – 24 + 1= 19.

Hence, 19 is Rakesh’s rank from the start.

Putting the codes in the given equation we have:

6² - 2² + 3² = 36 - 4 + 9 = 41 and

7² – 5² + 2² = 49 – 25 + 4 = 28

Similarly,

 5² – 3² + 1² = 25 – 9 + 1 = 17

Hence, 17 is the correct answer.

__
 
• The Jet engine works on the phenomenon of Conservation of Linear Momentum__.
 
• It produces a large volume of gases through the combustion of fuel, which is allowed to escape in backward direction through a jet.
 
• The backward rushing gas gains large momentum because of high velocity.
 
• It thus imparts an equal and opposite momentum to the jet engine.
 
• The jet engine, thus, moves forward with high speed.
 
• Conservation of Linear Momentum states that a body in motion retains its total momentum (product of mass and vector velocity) unless an external force is applied to it.

questions.question: What will happen to the level of water in a vessel when a piece of ice floating in it melts?

It will remain same and this phenomenon is explained by Archimedes Principle.

A floating object displaces an amount of water equal to its own weight. Since water expands when it freezes, one unit (of weight) of frozen water has a larger volume than one unit of liquid water. A completely submerged ice cube weighing one unit displaces more than one unit of liquid water. The cube will rise until the volume remaining under the surface displaces only one unit of water.

questions.question: Which of the following is CORRECT about coalition form of government?

options.text: Sharing of power at different levels
Sharing of power by different social groups
Sharing of power by two or more political parties

questions.solution:
A coalition government is a type of government where two or more political parties join together in parliament/ assembly to run the government and agree on a policy program.

 
• A coalition government is a cabinet of a parliamentary government in which several parties cooperate.
 
• The usual reason given for this arrangement is that no party on its own can achieve a majority in the parliament.
 
• A coalition government might also be created in a time of national difficulty or crisis, for example during wartime, to give a government the high degree of perceived political legitimacy it desires and also playing a role in diminishing internal political strife.
 
• In such times, parties have formed all-party coalitions (national unity governments, grand coalitions).
 
• If a coalition collapses a confidence vote is held or a motion of no confidence is taken.
 
• A coalition government is oftentimes considered a very weak form of government because there is no majority party.

Thus, we can say that a **coalition form of government means Sharing of power by two or more political parties.**

questions.question:

• In the given sentence, "had had" is used correctly as the** past perfect tense**.
 
• The past perfect tense is used to indicate that an action was completed before another action took place in the past. In this sentence, the action "had had a bad opinion of her" occurred before the action of meeting Sakshi.
 
• Let's break down the sentence to better understand the usage of "had had":
 
 
• Before I **met** Sakshi: This part of the sentence sets the context and establishes the** point in time in the past** when the action took place.
 
• I **had had** a bad opinion of her: This is the **past perfect tense**. The first "had" is the **auxiliary verb** and the second "had" is the **past participle** of the verb "have".
 
 
 
• The use of the **past perfect tense** emphasizes that the opinion was formed **before** the meeting took place. If we had used the simple past tense, the sentence would have been: "Before I met Sakshi, I had a bad opinion of her." This sentence would have conveyed the same meaning, but the past perfect tense emphasizes the sequence of events more clearly.
 
• In summary, "had had" is the past perfect tense and is used to show that an action was completed before another action in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **No improvement**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Mr. Gupta, his wife (1)/ and his younger brother (2)/ was present at the station. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Plural subjects** are always agreed upon by** plural verbs**.

 
 
• For example: My friends and I **were** going to the park.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, 'Mr Gupta, his wife and his younger brother' are **plural subjects**.
 
• Hence, the **verb** that must agree with them should also be** plural**.
 
• Thus, ‘was’ (singular verb) should be replaced by ‘were’ (plural verb).

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Mr. Gupta, his wife and his younger brother **were** present at the station.*

He gave me an additional _____ of Rs 800 a month by permission of the manager.
questions.solution:
‘Pay’ and ‘salary’ are dues given in exchange of some work. The given sentence does not convey any such meaning.

A ‘perquisite’ is a benefit which one enjoys or is entitled to on account of one's job or position. An ‘allowance’ is a sum granted as a reimbursement for expenses. The usage of ‘additional’ indicates that the concerned person was not *entitled *to the amount, but received it by permission of the manager. Thus, ‘allowance’ is the best fit answer.
